subject: surgery
title: Surgical endocrinopathies: primary hyperparathyroidism, pheochromocytoma, and adrenalectomy

steps.tx: Primary **hyperparathyroidism** (PHPT) is characterized by autonomous, uninhibited secretion of parathyroid hormone (PTH) producing hypercalcemia and hypophosphatemia. A single benign parathyroid adenoma accounts for 85 percent of cases, primary chief cell hyperplasia for 15 percent, and parathyroid carcinoma for under 1 percent. Classic clinical manifestations encompass painful bones, renal stones, abdominal groans, and psychic moans, though most modern patients present with asymptomatic hypercalcemia on routine screening.
steps.say: Primary hyperparathyroidism causes autonomous parathyroid hormone secretion, elevating serum calcium and lowering phosphate. A single adenoma accounts for 85 percent of cases, and four-gland hyperplasia for 15 percent. Symptoms include nephrolithiasis, bone disease, abdominal pain, and depression.

rows: Subtotal (3.5 gland) resection or total + auto-transplant
Bilateral neck exploration & excision of both
En bloc resection with ipsilateral thyroid lobectomy

steps.tx: Preoperative parathyroid **localization** utilizes sestamibi scintigraphy with single-photon emission CT (SPECT) and high-resolution cervical ultrasound. When concordant, these imaging modalities enable minimally invasive parathyroidectomy (MIP). Intraoperative parathyroid hormone (IOPTH) monitoring confirms complete resection via the Miami criterion: a drop in serum PTH of 50 percent or greater from baseline 10 minutes following adenoma excision, which carries a 98 percent cure rate.
steps.say: Parathyroid adenomas are localized preoperatively with ultrasound and sestamibi SPECT scans. Concordant imaging allows minimally invasive parathyroidectomy. Complete excision is confirmed intraoperatively by the Miami criterion: a 50 percent or greater PTH drop 10 minutes post-excision.

nodes.label: Concordant localization with ultrasound and sestamibi SPECT
Intraoperative PTH draw at baseline and 10 minutes post-excision
Confirm > 50 percent PTH drop indicating operative cure

steps.tx: Pheochromocytoma is a catecholamine-secreting **chromaffin** tumor arising from the adrenal medulla. Diagnosis is established by 24-hour urinary fractionated metanephrines or plasma free metanephrines. Preoperative pharmacological preparation is non-negotiable to avert lethal intraoperative hypertensive crisis. Alpha-adrenergic blockade (phenoxybenzamine) must be initiated 10 to 14 days prior to surgery; beta-adrenergic blockers are added ONLY after adequate alpha blockade to avoid unopposed alpha vasoconstriction.
steps.say: Pheochromocytoma arises from the adrenal medulla, secreting catecholamines. Diagnosis is confirmed by elevated metanephrines. Preoperative alpha-blockade with phenoxybenzamine is mandatory for 10 to 14 days; beta-blockers are added only after alpha blockade to prevent hypertensive crisis.

nodes.label: liberal salt and fluid intake to expand contracted intravascular volume
Add beta-blocker (propranolol) only after full alpha blockade
Laparoscopic adrenalectomy with early adrenal vein ligation

steps.tx: Laparoscopic transperitoneal or retroperitoneal **adrenalectomy** is the procedure of choice for benign functional adrenal tumors under 6 cm, including aldosteronomas (Conn syndrome), Cushing adenomas, and pheochromocytomas. Open adrenalectomy is mandated for suspected adrenal cortical carcinoma (ACC) or tumors exceeding 6 to 8 cm to achieve negative margins without capsular violation. Early ligation of the main adrenal vein is critical during pheochromocytoma resection to prevent hemodynamic instability.
steps.say: Laparoscopic adrenalectomy is the gold standard for benign functional tumors under 6 centimeters. Open adrenalectomy is indicated for suspected adrenocortical carcinoma or lesions larger than 6 centimeters. Early adrenal vein ligation prevents intraoperative catecholamine surges.

rows: Mixed hormone excess, large irregular mass > 6 cm
Open transabdominal radical en bloc adrenalectomy
